summary: Scheduler fallback generation limits now reserve the same EAGLE/NEXTN draft-token slots as tokenizer-side explicit-length validation. This closes a source-proven context-boundary gap for requests without max_tokens; the exact H800 TP8 crash remains unavailable for reproduction.

tests.what_was_measured: The old scheduler formula violated the four-slot speculative reserve at context_length=262144 and input_len=262091.
Nine tests and 542 parameterized boundary subtests passed, including speculative reserve and non-speculative/page/admission boundaries.
On the assigned AMD Instinct MI355X, 262091 + 49 + 4 equaled 262144 and an independent GPU reduction matched its CPU reference exactly.
Changed Python source and regression test compile successfully.

remaining_limitations: The assigned hardware was one AMD gfx950 GPU, not eight NVIDIA H800 GPUs.
CUDA, FA3 CUDA kernels, TP8, CUDA Graph replay, and the reported Xid 31 failure were not reproduced.
The result verifies a source-level boundary defect and its regression, not that this was the sole cause of the production crash.
